mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 130 P400 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Land Rover Defender 130 P400 engine typically costs between £4,500 and £10,000 for the supply-only unit, depending on the level of rebuild and specialist documentation provided.
- Rebuilt units include upgraded cooling components and timing chain checks.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our premium specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of cooling or timing chain failure in a Land Rover Defender 130 P400?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Land Rover Defender 130 P400 engine.
- Look for unexplained coolant loss, sudden overheating warnings, or a distinct rattling noise from the front of the engine at cold start.
- Sweet-smelling exhaust smoke or oil contamination are also strong indicators of internal failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a modern Land Rover Defender 130 P400?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, given the strong retained values of the L663 Defender 130, replacing the engine is a highly sound financial decision.
- A typical 2022+ model is valued between £65,000 and £95,000+, making a £6,500-£10,000 rebuild a small percentage of the vehicle's worth.
- A rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty adds reliability and protects your premium asset.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 130 P400 engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Land Rover Defender 130 P400 typically takes 3 to 5 days at a premium specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated and tested.
- Complex cases requiring additional cooling system upgrades may take slightly longer.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Land Rover Defender 130 to a P400 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While the L663 chassis was designed with multiple powertrain options, a retrofit is not straightforward.
- The P400 3.0L MHEV requires extensive ECU mapping, bespoke wiring harnesses, and upgraded cooling systems to function correctly and pass MOT.
- We strongly recommend sticking to a like-for-like replacement to ensure guaranteed compatibility, reliability, and warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 P400 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the stretched 8-seat Defender 130 officially launched in 2022, the P400 trim represented the pinnacle of modern JLR inline-six performance, pairing a 3.0-litre mild-hybrid petrol engine with the iconic long-wheelbase chassis for exceptional on-road refinement and robust off-road capability.

milestones.description: 3.0L I6 MHEV (P400), 395hp (400PS), launched alongside the new L663 Defender 130, featuring an integrated starter-generator (ISG) 48V mild-hybrid system and an electric supercharger for seamless torque fill.

Present - Continued production with exclusive special editions (e.g., 75th Edition, Carpathian Edition), maintaining the same robust 3.0L Ingenium petrol architecture with refined thermal management and calibration.

problems.group: Cooling System Leaks & Water Pump Wear
problems.h4: Cooling System Leaks & Water Pump Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 P400 3.0L I6 MHEV Requires Attention
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 130 P400 (3.0L I6 MHEV, 2022-present)
problems.rootCause: Plastic coolant fittings and water pump seals can degrade under high under-bonnet temperatures, leading to slow coolant loss and potential overheating if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace plastic coolant pipes with revised aluminium parts and update the water pump assembly.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended preventative maintenance to avoid catastrophic overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if neglect has led to severe overheating, warped heads, or deep mechanical knocking.

problems.recommendation: If the engine is fundamentally sound, addressing cooling components or the timing chain as preventative maintenance is highly cost-effective and preserves the original unit. However, if the vehicle has suffered severe overheating or exhibits deep mechanical knocking, a full reconditioned replacement is the only reliable path to protect your investment.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Stretch - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 P400 3.0L I6 MHEV Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Land Rover Defender 130 P400 (3.0L I6 MHEV, 2022-present)
problems.rootCause: High cylinder pressures and thermal cycling can cause premature wear on the timing chain guides and tensioners, resulting in a rattling noise at cold start.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip front covers, replace timing chain, guides, and tensioners with revised JLR specification parts.
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early before chain skip causes valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain failure has already caused internal valvetrain or piston damage.
